programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag
programme.desc: Nuair tha daolag-bhreac a’ tighinn air chèilidh, is a’ tilleadh air ais, is air ais, tha Fuigheag a’ dìon àite, agus gu h-àraidh a chuid bhìdh! When a ladybird comes to visit, and returns again, Fuigheag gets protective of his private space and, especially, his food!

programme.title: Sionnach agus Maigheach (Fox & Hare)
programme.desc: Tha Sionnach brònach nuair a chì e gun fheàrr le Maigheach a bhith a’ leughadh leabhar seach a bhith còmhla ris-san. Tha Tosg a’ moladh dhà e fhèin a chur ann an riochd ridire gaisgeil airson aire Maighich fhaighinn air ais. Tha an dithis aca a’ togail dràgon leis a’ bheachd gum faigh Sionnach buaidh air an dràgon, agus gun dearbh e a luach do Mhaigheach. When Hare would rather read her big book of fairytales than hang out with Fox, he fears he’s not exciting enough. According to Tusk, only by becoming a brave knight will Fox be able to prove the opposite is true. The two decide to build a dragon so Fox can beat it in battle and prove his worth to Hare.

programme.title: Ladybird & Bee/Daolag-bhreac is Seillean
programme.desc: Tha spòrs aig Daolag-bhreac is Seillean le rudan clòimhteach – cluich an t-Samhraidh. Ladybird and Bee play with fluffy things - summer play.

programme.title: Pompon Am Mathan Beag/Pompon Little Bear
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Pompon a’ faireachdainn nach eil sìon a' dol ceart dha, tha Dadaidh a' sealltainn dòigh dha air rudan a chur ceart! When Pompon feels that nothing is going right for him, Dadaidh shows him a way to sort things out!

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: ‘S e latha socair a th’ ann air an eilean, latha math airson a bhith dìomhain. Tha Àtaidh, Tilidh agus Nìp a’ crochadh hamag, is tha tòrr spòrs aca a’ feuchainn ri faighinn oirre. Tha na Boga-bogadaich a’ feuchainn ri faighinn oirre cuideachd, ach tha iad air an caith suas dhan adhar is a’ dol a-mach à sealladh. Càite an deach iad? Tha Àtaidh, Tilidh agus Nìp a’ falbh a’ lorg nam Boga-bogadach. It is a lazy day on the Island. Abney, Teal and Neep put up a hammock and have a great time trying to get into it. The Poc-Pocs join in the fun but are thrown up into the air and disappear. Where have they gone? Abney, Teal and Neep go on a Poc-Poc hunt.

programme.title: Dan & Gran
programme.desc: Grandad is in Gran's good books for tidying his desk, but he tells Stan that it wasn't him! Who are the mystery tidy-uppers and how did they get in? Tha Gran toilicht' leis an t-Seanair leis gun do sgioblaich e 'n deasg aige, ach e 'g ràdh ri Dan nach b' esan a sgioblaich e. Ach cò an luchd-glanaidh dìomhair, agus ciamar a nochd iad an seo?

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Catriona Nic a’ Phì a’ leughadh Mar a Chuireas tu Leòmhann air Falach. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh agus a dhealbhachadh le Helen Stephens agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Morag Stiùbhart. A bedtime story for young children. Catriona MacPhee reads Mar a Chuireas tu Leòmhann air Falach, written and illustrated by Helen Stephens and translated into Gaelic by Morag Stewart.

programme.title: Hilda
programme.desc: Tha Hilda a’ dol gu coinneamh nan Sgùdan Sporais ’son a’ chiad turas, is tha bràiste ri chosnadh. Tha i fhèin ’s a caraidean dol a sgioblachadh sa phàirc. Chan eil gnothaichean ag obrachadh mar a shaoileadh tu, ge-ta! Hilda goes to a Sparrow Scouts meeting for the first time, and there is a badge to be earned. She and her friends tidy up in the park, but things don’t work out as you would imagine!

programme.title: Oidhche Shamhna CBBC ALBA
programme.desc: Tanith Rothach le taghadh a tha eagalach fhèin math airson Oidhche Shamhna, le slaidhm, braimeannan agus taibhse no dhà cuideachd! Tanith Munro introduces some frighteningly good highlights for Halloween, with slime, farts and a ghost or two!

programme.title: A-null ’s a-nall
programme.desc: Nuair a tha aig Minho ri fuireach airson greiseag aig taigh Granaidh, chan eil a’ chùis ri còrdadh ris. Tha e taingeil, ge-tà, gu bheil Mango, a charaid, còmhla ris. When Minho has to stay at Granny’s for a while, he isn’t happy. He is, however, glad that his friend Mango is with him.

programme.title: Geamaichean Gorach
programme.desc: Tha sinn a’ coinneachadh ri Coinneach Clogaid, Olaidh Orains – oh, agus tha sinn a’ tighinn tarsainn air comharra-clisge ann an àite neònach. We meet Coinneach Clogaid, Olaidh Orains and we come upon an exclamation mark in a strange place.

programme.title: Geamaichean Gorach
programme.desc: Tha Olaidh Orains agus Màiri Bhàn nan Casan Fada fìor mhath air spèileadh ach tha a gruag gam fàgail ann an snaimeannan! Olaidh Orains and Mairi Bhàn have lots of dance moves as they ice skate, but her long hair leaves them in knots!

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Serie A (BBC Alba)
programme.desc: Tha sinn ann an Turin le ball-coise Eadailteach le Torino a’ cluiche Como beò ann an Serie A. We head to Turin for live Italian football as Torino face Como in Serie A.

programme.title: Alba fon Talamh/Scotland Underground
programme.desc: In the Highlands and Islands, Calum explores the caves of Assynt, a Unesco global geopark, before travelling north to Orkney where there is a wealth of archeological underground sites. But it is also an example of the modern use of subterranean sites: oil to service the Scapa Flow naval sites was hidden underground in vast tanks beneath Wee Fea hill. The war theme continues as Calum visits a Cold War underground bunker in Inverness. Anns a’ Ghàidhealtachd agus na h-Eileanan, bheir Calum cuairt tro uamhan Asainte, geò-pàirc cruinneil UNESCO. À sin, thèid e tuath gu Arcaibh far a bheil beartas de làraich arceòlach fon talamh, ach cuideachd eisimpleir nas ùire den fho-thalamh a chleachdadh. Fo chnoc Wee Fea, tha na tancaichean mòra a bha a’ cumail ola ri làrach a’ Chabhlaich Rìoghail ann an Scapa Flow. A’ cumail ri tèama a’ chogaidh, ann an Inbhirnis tadhlaidh Calum air buncair bho àm a’ Chogaidh Fhuair. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Rùm Gu Rùm, Le Erica
programme.desc: Tha Erica Nic a’ Phearsain air ais a’ toirt cruth-atharrachadh àlainn air seòmaran agus toglaichean le a dealbhachadh sònraichte. Leanaidh sinn i bho thoiseach gu deireadh phròiseactan is sinn a’ faicinn gach pàirt den phròiseas, bho phlana air pàipear gu bhith a’ trusadh stuthan airson crìoch snasail a chur orra. Interior designer Erica MacPherson is back to transform more rooms, homes and businesses. We follow her process from architectural plans to trawling auction houses and shops for finishing touches. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Fonn mo Bheatha
programme.desc: Ceòl agus còmhradh le Cathy Ann Nic a Phi còmhla ri Jenna Cumming. Music and chat programme presented by Cathy Ann MacPhee with guest Jenna Cumming.

programme.title: Alleluia!
programme.desc: Psalm 91 air a sheinn le Còisir Ghàidhlig Bhaile Ghobhainn, an laoidh 'Reul Àlainn a' Chuain' le Kathleen Ghreumach agus bidh Mairead NicSuain ag innse mun phàirt a th' aig creideamh na beatha fhèin. Tha am prògram air aithris le Iain MacFhionghain. Govan Gaelic Choir sings Psalm 91, Kathleen Graham sings the hymn 'Reul Àlainn a' Chuain' and Margaret MacSween tells her personal faith story. Presented by Iain MacKinnon.

programme.title: Meaban and Moo
programme.desc: Bidh Linda a’ tadhal air a caraidean Meaban is Moo sa bhothan aca gus dùbhlain spòrsail a chur romhpa. Seo tha i ag iarraidh orra trì diofar ghlasraich a lorg fhad ’s a tha iad cuideachd a' dèanamh deiseil airson partaidh Oidhche Shamhna. Tha treallaich gu leòr sa bhothan agus feumaidh Meaban is Moo a dhol a rùrach! Linda visits her friends Meaban and Moo at their hut to set them fun challenges. She tasks them with finding three different vegetables while they get ready for a Halloween party. Their hut is full of junk, so Meaban and Moo just need to have a good rummage!

programme.title: Leum Suas air an Sguaib/Room on the Broom
programme.desc: Tha Lìosaidh NicÌosaig, a' bhana-bhuidseach, 's an cat gu dòigheil a' seòladh air sguab. Tha a' ghaoth mhòr ag èirigh 's tha Lìosaidh a' call a h-ad, an rioban a tha na falt, 's an t-slatag a tha na làimh. Ge-ta, tha triùir charaidean eile a' nochdadh a bheir taic dhi. The witch and the cat fly through the sky on a broomstick. The wind picks up, the witch drops her hat, her bow and her wand. Fortunately, three more friends come to her aid. Can they rescue the witch from the dragon and will there be room on the broom for all?

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Le taic bho chàch, tha Pipp a’ dol na banrigh, le crùn, cathair agus parèid rìoghail. With a bit of Froggie help, Pipp turns into a queen with crown, throne and royal parade.

programme.title: Dan & Gran
programme.desc: Grandad is in Gran's good books for tidying his desk, but he tells Stan that it wasn't him! Who are the mystery tidy-uppers and how did they get in? Tha Gran toilicht' leis an t-Seanair leis gun do sgioblaich e 'n deasg aige, ach e 'g ràdh ri Dan nach b' esan a sgioblaich e. Ach cò an luchd-glanaidh dìomhair, agus ciamar a nochd iad an seo?

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Tha Peicein is a charaidean gann de dh’airgead, is leis nach eil ann an airgead ach pìosan beaga pàipeir le dealbhan orra, tha iad uile a’ co-dhùnadh gun cruthaich iad an t-airgead aca fhèin, is gun ceannaich iad na thogras iad. Because they are a little short of money, and considering cash notes are only little papers with drawings on them, Petit and his friends decide to create their own money and buy anything they want.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Martainn Mac an t-Saoir a’ leughadh Am Balach a bha ag Ithe Leabhraichean. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh agus a dhealbhachadh le Oliver Jeffers agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. A bedtime story for young children. Martin MacIntyre reads Am Balach a bha ag Ithe Leabhraichean, written and illustrated by Oliver Jeffers and translated into Gaelic by Donald John MacLeod.

programme.title: Calum: Cogadh nan Comhlan
programme.desc: Tha Calum airson a chòmhlann aige a thoirt à Glaschu dhan Òban airson blàr mòr ciùil a tha dol aig a' Mhòd Nàiseanta Rìoghail. Ach, le tòrr fharpaisean agus gainead tìde, chan eil cùisean a' dol mar bu chòir. Leis nach eil e furasda còmhlan a làimhseachadh aig na h-amannan as fheàrr, saoil ciamar a thèid dhaibh leis na dùbhlain mhòra a th' air thoiseach orra... Calum aims to take his band from Glasgow to Oban for a major musical battle at the Royal National Mòd. However, with numerous competitions and time constraints, things aren't going according to plan. Managing a band is never easy even in the best of times - how will they cope with the significant challenges that lie ahead?

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc: The beul gun phutan Lynette ag adhbharachadh cunnart airson Elaina. Ciamar a gheibh Belle, Sebastian agus na caraidean air cùisean a shàbhaladh? Lynette’s loose lips puts Elaina in danger. How can Belle, Sebastian and the gang save the day?

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Leis an tuathanach agus Bitzer a' falbh a-mach airson latha còmhla ri chèile, tha Seonaidh a' gabhail a' chothruim a bhith os cionn ghnothaichean. Ach tha e a' mothachadh gu math luath nach eil an obair cho furasta 's a bha e an dùil. When the farmer decides it is time he and Bitzer head out for a bit of man and dog time, Shaun seizes his chance to take charge. He soon discovers that the job is not quite as easy as he first thought.

programme.title: Flix
programme.desc: Tha Flix 'son dearbhadh g’ eil easan na shàr chat feireil – dìreach mar athair, Zeno. Chan eil a nàmhaid, Burma, dol a dhèanamh chùisean furasta dha, ge-tà! Flix wants to prove that he’s an ultimate outdoor cat - just like his dad, Zeno. However his nemesis Burma isn’t going to make things easy for him!

programme.title: Golf: Mun Cuairt Alba
programme.desc: Cùrsaichean ann an Lodainn an Ear, is coidse le comhairle. The 15th Redan hole at North Berwick and golf tips from Keil Beveridge.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Joy Dunlop a’ leantainn oirre gar toirt tro thuilleadh cheumannan gus Gàidhlig a bhruidhinn. Joy Dunlop continues to guide us through further steps to speak Gaelic.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Rathad Ramsay
programme.desc: Ramsay meets Ian Smith in the village he was brought up, before they head along one of Tiree’s most famous beaches. As they walk along the coast, Ian reflects on his youth and the people that impacted him. Ian discusses how the Tiree music scene shaped him and brought him success as a box player, and he shares his passion for the island and his pride in setting up the only distillery in Tiree. San treas sreath de Rathad Ramsay bidh Ramsay MacMahon a’ coinneachadh ri sàr Ghàidheil bho air feadh Alba ‘s iad a’ co-roinn sgeulachdan, cuir luach air nàdar agus a’ cnuasachadh ma beatha. Coinnichidh Ramsay ri Iain Mac a’ Ghobhainn sa bhaile san d’rugadh e mas dèan iad air tè de na tràighean as iomraitiche ann an Tiriodh. Meòirichidh Iain air làithean òige agus na daoine bu mhotha a thug buaidh air a bheatha. Leis cho cudromach ‘s a tha ceòl air eilean Thiriodh, innsidh Iain man bhuaidh a bh’aige seo air fhèin agus mar a chuidich e a bhith cho soirbheachail le cluich a’ bhogsa. Bidh an dà chuid a mheas air an eilean agus a mhoit man aon taigh-stàile san eilean fhaighinn stèidhichte follaiseach. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Sailm nan Daoine
programme.desc: Tha an ceòladair Rob MacNeacail air turas gus cumhachd seinn nan salm Gàidhlig a sgaoileadh. Musician Rob MacNeacail is on a mission to spread the power of Gaelic psalm singing.

programme.title: Dàna | Scotland's Wild Side
programme.desc: The vast landscape of the Cairngorms attracts thousands each year. Coinneach Rankin sets out on a multi-day expedition to learn why its vast mountains are a paradise for climbers, runners and so many others. Along with his partner, Coinneach races up one of the highest mountains in Scotland, undertakes a classic multi-pitch climb, and spends the night in a tiny bothy built in the 1960s. Tàlaidh cruth-tìre aibheiseach a’ Mhonaidh Ruaidh na mìltean gach bliadhna. Cuiridh Coinneach MacFhraing aghaidh air turas grunn làithean gus tuigsinn carson a tha sreapadairean, luchd-coise agus eile cho measail air na beanntan seo. An cuideachd deagh charaid, thèid Coinneach na dheann suas tè de na beanntan as àirde an Alba, dìreidh e slighe-sreapa fhada agus cuiridh e seachad na h-oidhche ann am bothan a thogadh ‘sna seasgadan. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Ath-thogail Notre-Dame/Rebuilding Notre-Dame
programme.desc: A year after a major fire, archaeologists and scientists examine the battered stones of Notre-Dame in Paris.

programme.title: Skipinnish Aig A' Chaisteal
programme.desc: Skipinnish le December ann an cuideachd na mìltean de luchd-leantainn aig cuirm-chiùil a’ comharrachadh 25 bliadhna de Skipinnish, bho Chaisteal Dhùn Èideann. Skipinnish perform December in front of thousands of fans at a concert celebrating 25 years of the band, from Edinburgh Castle.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Bing a’ cluich geama le fòn-làimhe Flop, chaneil rudan a’ dol mar bu chòir oir tha am fòn-làimhe a' briseadh nuair a tha e dol na sgeing air an làr. An àite seo innse do Flop, tha Bing ga chuir dhan bhiona. Tha e faireachdainn cho dona mun seo ach tha e ag ionnsachadh gum feum e innse mar a thachair. When Bing is playing a game with Flop’s mobile phone, he accidentally drops the mobile and it breaks. Instead of telling Flop, he throws it in the bin. He feels upset about it all and learns that it’s best to tell the truth.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Bing aig cuirm sa phàirc, tha còir aige 'n oidhch' a chrìochnachadh ach tha e air bhioran agus tha e fàs cho diùid. Ge-tà, le taic bho charaidean, tha e faighinn seachad air na duilgheadasan sin agus tha e a' seinn Òran a’ Bhogha-fhroise. When Bing is at a show in the park, he is extremely nervous as he is meant to be singing the finale. However, with help from his friends, Bing gets over all his insecurities and sings the Rainbow Song.

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: Tha Ben a' leughadh sgeulachd dha na h-Abadas mus tig iad dhan leabaidh. Aig deireadh na sgeòil, tha iad airson an geama fhaclan a chlcuich, 's tha Hari ga fhaighinn fhèin sa ghàrradh a' coimhead son cailleach-oidhche. Before going to bed, Ben reads Seren, Hari and Ela a story. When the story ends, the Abadas decide to play the word game and this sends Hari to a windy garden looking for an owl.

programme.desc: ‘S e latha socair a th’ ann air an eilean, latha math airson a bhith dìomhain. Tha Àtaidh, Tilidh agus Nìp a’ crochadh hamag, is tha tòrr spòrs aca a’ feuchainn ri faighinn oirre. The Poc-Pocs join in the fun but are thrown up into the air and disappear. Where have they gone? Abney, Teal and Neep go on a Poc-Poc hunt.

programme.title: ’S E Iasg a Th’Annam (I’m a Fish)
programme.desc: Ged a tha riochd caran neo-àbhaisteach air a’ Bhagan-mhara, tha e den bheachd gu bheil cuid eile ann an tha nas grainnde buileach na iad. Although the Blobfish looks rather unusual, he says that there are other fish who are even more aesthetically displeasing than him.

programme.title: Peataichean/Pets
programme.desc: Tha Eilidh NicCarmaig a’ coinneachadh ri clann agus a’ faighinn a-mach mu mar a tha iad a’ coimhead às dèidh agus a’ cluich cuide rim peataichean aig an taigh. Anns a’ phrògram seo tha Eilidh a’ cèilidh air Emily agus na coineanaich aice, Syrius agus Seumas a tha beothail agus bòidheach. Gheibh sinn a-mach barrachd mu bhith a’ coimhead às dèidh coineanaich agus mu na rudan snog is spòrsail a bhios iad a’ dèanamh còmhla. Gheibh sinn cuideachd comhairle agus fiosrachadh bho Eilidh fhèin mu bhith a’ làimhseachadh, ag oideachadh agus a’ coimhead às dèidh peataichean. Eilidh Cormack meets young children who are pet owners. Together they show, tell and share how they care for, play and interact with their pets at home. In this episode, Eilidh visits Emily and her adorable rabbits, Syrius and Seumas. We find out how to look after rabbits and about all the lovely stuff Emily, Syrius and Seumas get up to together. Eilidh also shares fun and interesting facts along with advice on looking after pets at home; including how best to handle, train and feed them.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Dòmhnall Ruadh a’ leughadh An Ròn Beag. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Janis Mackay agus a dhealbhachadh le Gabby Grant. Chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Jo NicDhòmhnaill. A bedtime story for young children. Donald Smith reads An Ròn Beag by Janis Mackay, illustrated by Gabby Grant and translated into Gaelic by Jo Macdonald.

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Gealach na Durraige Guirme a' nochdadh, tha i a’ taladh dhurragan gorma a tha glè thearc, ach blasta, agus ma dh'itheas Gumbal tè dhiubh, tha a h-uile càil a' dol ceàrr! When the Blue Grub Moon appears, it brings out a very rare but delicious grub and if a Gumbal eats one, things go wrong!

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Troig is Bonns a’ feuchainn ri Gumbal-sgluidseadh, tha tubaist ann is tha iad suainte ri chèile. Feumar obrachadh còmhla ach ciamar a gheibh na caraidean air adhart leis a seo? When Troig and Bonns try to gumblesplat, they accidentally get entwined. They have to work together, but how will the friends get on with this?

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Leis an tuathanach agus Bitzer a' falbh a-mach airson latha còmhla ri chèile, tha Seonaidh a' gabhail a' chothruim a bhith os cionn ghnothaichean. She and her friends tidy up in the park, but things don’t work out as you would imagine!

programme.title: Seòid a' Chidsin - The Kitchen Coves
programme.desc: Tha na seòid a’ cleachdadh mustard eadar-dhealaichte gus truinnsearan inntinneach a chruthachadh. Tha ùidh aig Ruairidh ann am mustard a tha ga dhèanamh sna Hearadh agus ag iarraidh air Ùisdean reòiteag a dhèanamh leis! Tha Ùisdean a’ toirt sùil air ais air reasabaidh traidiseanta airson slios feòla le mustard, air a ghabhail le buntàta Hasselback Ruairidh. Tha Ruairidh cuideachd ag ullachadh Cearc Supreme agus a’ cur crìoch air a’ phrògram le Carpaccio Bhiotais. The lads use different mustards to make a variety of dishes. Ruaridh is inspired by a Harris-made mustard and asks Uisdean to make ice cream, using the mustard! Uisdean looks back at a traditional recipe for Flank with mustard, accompanied by Ruaridh’s Hasselback potatoes. Ruairidh also prepares a classic, chicken supreme, and finishes off the episode with a beetroot carpaccio. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Joy Dunlop leads us on our Gaelic learning journey. Dr Teàrlach Wilson joins her in the studio, and Calum Maclean visits Govan while on the hunt for a collection of stones.

programme.title: Cidsin Granaidh Chalanais
programme.desc: Gregor MacLeod takes on the classics shortbread and marmalade. Grannie has five recipes for shortbread alone, but Gregor has to pick just one.

programme.title: Ath-thogail Notre-Dame/Rebuilding Notre-Dame
programme.desc: In 2019, a catastrophic fire threatened Notre-Dame’s structure. Analysing the vaults of the building, researchers unveil its history and decipher the secrets of its past resistance.

programme.title: Abigail
programme.desc: Mar annlann a tha na thrèat air leth, tha Abigail a' dèanamh Briosgaidean Seasaman Tahini. Glè, glè bhlasta, a' brùchdadh le deagh bhlas is teòclaid geal! For a splendid accompaniment treat, Abigail makes tahini sesame cookies. Very tasty, packed with flavour and white chocolate! In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Sailm nan Daoine
programme.desc: Tha an ceòladair Rob MacNeacail air turas gus cumhachd seinn nan salm Gàidhlig a sgaoileadh. Musician Rob MacNeacail is on a mission to spread the power of Gaelic psalm singing.

programme.title: OMC!
programme.desc: A sketch show featuring a collection of comic characters, spoofs, inappropriate dates and a snapshot of the past. Written by and starring the very best in emerging and established comic talent. Featuring Iain Beggs, Darren Maclean, Carina Macleod, Claire Frances MacNeil, Hannah McKirdy, Lana Pheutan and David Walker. Includes sharpened words between mother and daughter in law, a new guy at work discovers what makes the office tick, and it’s eyes down for a coveted prize at the bingo. Anns an treas prògram bho shreath ùr OMC! chì sinn tuilleadh sgeidsichean loma-làn charactaran èibhinn, suidheachaidhean neònach agus ‘spoofs’ gun shamhail bho n sgrìobhadairean is cleasaichean as fheàrr a th’ann. An turas sa mòmaidean ain-fhoiseil le màthair cèile, duilgheadasan cainnt ann an obair ùr, agus duais air leth ri thogail aig am bingo! In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: Tha Ben a' leughadh sgeulachd dha na h-Abadas mus tig iad dhan leabaidh. Aig deireadh na sgeòil, tha iad airson an geama fhaclan a chlcuich, 's tha Hari ga fhaighinn fhèin sa ghàrradh a' coimhead son cailleach-oidhche. Before going to bed, Ben reads Seren, Hari and Ela a story. When the story ends, the Abadas decide to play the word game and this sends Hari to a windy garden looking for an owl.

programme.title: Meaban and Moo
programme.desc: Bidh Linda a’ tadhal air a caraidean Meaban is Moo sa bhothan aca gus dùbhlain spòrsail a chur romhpa. Seo tha i ag iarraidh orra trì diofar ghlasraich a lorg fhad ’s a tha iad cuideachd a' dèanamh deiseil airson partaidh Oidhche Shamhna. Tha treallaich gu leòr sa bhothan agus feumaidh Meaban is Moo a dhol a rùrach! Linda visits her friends Meaban and Moo at their hut to set them fun challenges. She tasks them with finding three different vegetables while they get ready for a Halloween party. Their hut is full of junk, so Meaban and Moo just need to have a good rummage!

programme.title: Leum Suas air an Sguaib/Room on the Broom
programme.desc: Tha Lìosaidh NicÌosaig, a' bhana-bhuidseach, 's an cat gu dòigheil a' seòladh air sguab. Tha a' ghaoth mhòr ag èirigh 's tha Lìosaidh a' call a h-ad, an rioban a tha na falt, 's an t-slatag a tha na làimh. Ge-ta, tha triùir charaidean eile a' nochdadh a bheir taic dhi. The witch and the cat fly through the sky on a broomstick. The wind picks up, the witch drops her hat, her bow and her wand. Fortunately, three more friends come to her aid. Can they rescue the witch from the dragon and will there be room on the broom for all?

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Mairi Mairi NicAongais a' leughadh Bana-phrionnsa a' Phoca Phàipeir. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Robert Munsch agus a dhealbhachadh le Michael Martchenko. Chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Jo NicDhòmhnaill. A bedtime story for young children. Mairi MacInnes reads Bana-phrionnsa a’ Phoca Phàipeir by Robert Munsch, illustrated by Michael Martchenko and translated into Gaelic by Jo Macdonald.

programme.title: SpongeBob
programme.desc: Tha Mgr. Crùbag air a chlisgeadh mun sgrùdadh slàinte aige. Mr Krabs is too scared to get his physical.

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc: Ged a tha na saor-làithean air tòiseachadh do sgoilearan Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche, tha latha a bharrachd aig an luchd-teagaisg airson beagan trèanaidh. Tha an t-eòlaiche-inntinn Sìleas Stern os cionn sheiseanan gus sìth agus càirdeas a stèidheachadh am measg an luchd-obrach. Although the holidays have started for the pupils of Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche, the teachers have an in-service day. Mr Mackle is keen to establish better relationships between his staff and has invited psychologist Sìleas Stern to run team building sessions that he hopes will bring peace and harmony.

programme.title: Calum: Cogadh nan Comhlan
programme.desc: Tha Calum airson a chòmhlann aige a thoirt à Glaschu dhan Òban airson blàr mòr ciùil a tha dol aig a' Mhòd Nàiseanta Rìoghail. Ach, le tòrr fharpaisean agus gainead tìde, chan eil cùisean a' dol mar bu chòir. Leis nach eil e furasda còmhlan a làimhseachadh aig na h-amannan as fheàrr, saoil ciamar a thèid dhaibh leis na dùbhlain mhòra a th' air thoiseach orra... Calum aims to take his band from Glasgow to Oban for a major musical battle at the Royal National Mòd. However, with numerous competitions and time constraints, things aren't going according to plan. Managing a band is never easy even in the best of times - how will they cope with the significant challenges that lie ahead?

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc: Nuair tha Camshron a' tighinn tarsainn air ugh iolair-dhubh, tha e airson an t-ugh a chumail dha fhèin. Tha e cho rag. Ciamar a gheibh na seòid air an ugh a thilleadh don nead 's a chumail sàbhailt’? When Cameron comes across a black eagle’s egg, he wants to keep the egg for himself - he is so stubborn! How will the gang manage to return the egg to the nest and keep it safe?

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Tha an tuathanach a' co-dhùnadh gu bheil an t-àm ann fàs fallain - agus tha e ag iarraidh Bitzer a thoirt a-steach air cùisean. Tha beachd eile aig Bitzer ge-tà agus tha e a' tighinn an àrd le plana dìomhair gus an obair chruaidh a sheachnadh. An dèan an sgeama aige a' chùis aig a' cheann thall? The farmer decides it is time to get fit and calls on Bitzer to join him. Bitzer has other ideas and comes up with a secret plan to avoid putting in the hard work. Will his scheme catch up with him in the end?

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Abigail
programme.desc: 'S e th' ann am Brot fìor bhlast' de Choiridh leantail, ach lòn sònraicht' nach dìochuimhnich thu ann an cabhaig. An extremely delicious curried lentil soup is a special lunch which you won't forget in a hurry. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Fonn mo Bheatha
programme.desc: Ceòl agus còmhradh le Cathy Ann Nic a Phi còmhla ri Jenna Cumming. Music and chat programme presented by Cathy Ann MacPhee with guest Jenna Cumming.

programme.title: Gàrraidhean Mòra na h-Alba
programme.desc: Murdo Macdonald explores Ardkinglas Gardens in Argyll. Murchadh Dòmhnallach a’cur eòlas air Gàrradh Àird Chonghlais ann an Earra-Ghaidheal.

programme.title: Cuirm aig Celtic
programme.desc: Ceòl is còmhradh bho cuirm shònraichte le Sian aig Celtic Connections. Anns a’ buidheann Ghàidhlig Albannach, tha triùir dhen na seinneadairean Gàidhlig as fheàrr – Eilidh NicCarmaig, Ceitlin Lilidh & Ellen NicDhòmhnaill – le luchd-ciùil eile nan cois gus an dàrna clàr aca a thaisbeanadh beò ann an dòigh nach cualas roimhe. Air a lìbhrigeadh le Megan NicGill-Fhaolain. Music and conversation from Sian’s concert at Celtic Connections to celebrate the release of their second album. The Scottish Gaelic folk group comprises three of today’s top Gaelic singers - Eilidh Cormack, Ceitlin Lilidh and Ellen MacDonald - who are joined by an extended line-up of musicians to perform the album live as never before. Presented by Megan MacLellan. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: An Geam Àlainn
programme.desc: Ball-coise nam ban ann an Alba bho shealladh luchd-cluiche, luchd-leantainn & eòlaichean. Women’s football in Scotland seen through the eyes of players, fans and experts.

programme.title: Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean/Wild Senses
programme.desc: Ann an saoghal làn gleadhraich, ciamar a tha beathaichean a’ dèanamh ciall dheth? In a world filled with noise, how do animals make sense of it all?

programme.title: Skipinnish Aig A' Chaisteal
programme.desc: Skipinnish le December ann an cuideachd na mìltean de luchd-leantainn aig cuirm-chiùil a’ comharrachadh 25 bliadhna de Skipinnish, bho Chaisteal Dhùn Èideann. Skipinnish perform December in front of thousands of fans at a concert celebrating 25 years of the band, from Edinburgh Castle.

programme.title: Skerryvore Aig Caisteal Floors
programme.desc: Prògram sònraichte a’ comharrachadh 20 bliadhna de Skerryvore. Chùm an còmhlan ainmeil Albannach cuirm shònraichte do nam mìltean de luchd-leantainn ann an àrainn àlainn Caisteal Floors sna Crìochan. Le agallamhan leis a’ chòmhlan is caraidean agus le criomagan bhon chonsairt. A special programme to celebrate 20 years of Skerryvore. The legendary Scottish band performed an anniversary show to thousands of fans in the spectacular surroundings of Floors Castle in the Scottish Borders. Featuring interviews with band members and friends, plus concert highlights. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Ancient Worlds
programme.desc: In the last of the series, archaeologist and historian Richard Miles examines the rise and fall of the Roman Empire. At the height of its power, the Roman Empire extended the benefits of its civilisation to 60 million citizens and subjects in a swathe of territory that extended from Hadrian's Wall to the banks of the Euphrates. Even under the rule of mad, bad and dangerous emperors, the imperial system proved to be robust, buttressed by the support of elite families in the far-flung corners of the empire, whose loyalty was ensured by a system of cultural aspiration, economic opportunity and military coercion. But the material benefits of the 'good order' delivered by Roman rule provided its citizens and subjects with the security to ask profound questions about the meaning of life - questions that the pragmatic, polytheistic Roman belief system was ill-equipped to answer. Christianity grew to fill the spiritual vacuum at the heart of Roman civilisation, eventually claiming an emperor, Constantine, as its greatest prize. The City of Man would be eclipsed the City of God.

programme.title: The Latest Secrets of Hieroglyphs
programme.desc: The great history of Egypt is inscribed on its monuments, temples and tombs, but hieroglyphs – the written language of the ancient Egyptians – fell silent until 1822 when a young French scholar, Jean-François Champollion, became the first person to decipher their texts for over a thousand years. Champollion’s insights and the work of other scholars helped bring an entire civilisation back to life. Today, researchers are increasingly interested in the authors who created these hieroglyphic works. Near Luxor, we follow a new generation of Egyptologists as they unlock the texts inscribed inside a richly adorned tomb, revealing the beliefs and lives of the priests, scribes, painters, engravers and builders who created this grand funerary monument.

programme.title: New Zealand: Earth's Mythical Islands
programme.desc: New Zealand was one of the last land masses to be found and settled by people. Lush and fertile, almost everything brought here flourishes, often with surprising consequences. Told through the experiences of its native species - in particular, a charismatic and peculiar giant, flightless parrot - this is the moving story of the changing fortunes of New Zealand's wildlife since humans first arrived.

programme.title: Secrets of Skin
programme.desc: What makes sharks built for speed? How do snakes move without limbs? How do sugar gliders fly without feathers? The answer all lies in their skin. Professor Ben Garrod uncovers the secrets of how skin has evolved to enable animals to solve some of the most remarkable challenges on earth. To do this, Ben heads to the specialist flight centre at the Royal Veterinary College to analyse the way a sugar glider uses its skin flaps to stay aloft. He goes diving with sharks at the Blue Planet Aquarium and discovers that, far from being smooth, sharkskin is incredibly rough. It is covered with thousands of tiny teeth that make a shark hydrodynamic. Ben also finds out how the keratinised scales on snakes' bellies are the perfect configuration to allow them to move over virtually any surface they encounter.

programme.title: Gareth Edwards’s Great Welsh Adventure
programme.desc: Shire horses, lifeboat heroes and a rugby team who train on the beach are among friends old and new that Gareth and Maureen Edwards meet on a trip away to St Davids, Pembrokeshire.

programme.title: To the Manor Born
programme.desc: Stately sitcom. Audrey upbraids Richard for not sponsoring a charity event in aid of a new scout hut.

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances
programme.desc: Hyacinth has decided that, instead of her usual gift to Richard of slippers, he should receive skis instead. When Richard protests that he has no intention of taking up the sport, Hyacinth responds that he can cultivate the correct image by strapping them atop the car and drive about with them occasionally.

programme.title: The Normans
programme.desc: In the second of this three-part series, Professor Robert Bartlett explores the impact of the Norman conquest of Britain and Ireland. Bartlett shows how William the Conqueror imposed a new aristocracy, savagely cut down opposition and built scores of castles and cathedrals to intimidate and control. He also commissioned the Domesday Book, the greatest national survey of England that had ever been attempted. England adapted to its new masters and both the language and culture were transformed as the Normans and the English intermarried. Bartlett shows how the political and cultural landscape of Scotland, Wales and Ireland were also forged by the Normans and argues that the Normans created the blueprint for colonialism in the modern world.

programme.title: Storyville
programme.desc: The remarkable story of Kwame Brathwaite, the Harlem photographer, activist and cultural pioneer whose work helped define the iconic Black Is Beautiful movement. Across a career spanning more than seven decades, Kwame captured over 500,000 images documenting African American life, creativity and identity, while championing black pride through photography, fashion and grassroots activism. Featuring exclusive archive material and contributions from family members, artists and cultural figures including Alicia Keys, Swizz Beatz, Gabrielle Union and Jesse Williams, this documentary explores Brathwaite’s pivotal role in reshaping perceptions of black beauty and culture around the world.

programme.title: Light and Dark
programme.desc: Professor Jim Al-Khalili tells the story of how we went from thinking we were close to a complete understanding of the universe to realising we had seen almost none of it.

programme.title: How the Romans Conquered the Alps
programme.desc: In 15BC, the Emperor Augustus set out to conquer Germania, but to pacify this northern territory, he needed to control a direct route through the unconquered Alps. Despite its importance, little was known about Augustus’s Alpine campaign until researchers uncovered an ancient battlefield and the Roman Empire’s highest military camp at the Septimer Pass in the Swiss canton of Grisons. A team of archaeologists, forensic and ballistics experts reconstruct the campaign, revealing for the first time the route, weapons and tactics used to overcome the Suanetes. The findings reveal how Roman soldiers coped in the harsh mountain conditions to successfully annex much of the Alps in a single summer. This province, Raetia, remained under Roman control for 400 years.

programme.title: Building Sights
programme.desc: Architect Sand Helsel applauds Trellick Tower, a brutalist tower block in west London, designed by Erno Goldfinger and completed in 1972.

programme.title: The Singing Detective
programme.desc: Marlow is getting better, and the different strands of his fiction and reality begin to occupy the same time and place.

programme.title: The Singing Detective
programme.desc: The young Philip Marlow returns to the country railway station following his mother's death in London. Forty years on, Marlow the hospital patient still dreams about the homecoming and the frightening figure of the scarecrow that now erupts into the ward.

programme.title: Timewatch
programme.desc: Documentary that re-examines the attempt to blow up the Houses of Parliament in 1605 - one of the most famous yet least understood events in British history. It shows how the plot was almost England's 9/11, and asks why a group of young Englishmen became so radicalised and so hell-bent on terrorism. Computer graphics recreate what the Houses of Parliament looked like in 1605, and show just how close the plotters came to success.

programme.title: Battlefield Britain
programme.desc: Dan Snow experiences how the Battle of Britain was fought at the limits of human endurance when he takes flight in a high performance stunt plane. Recreating the spiralling turns of a dogfight, he feels the extraordinary side-effects of the high G forces felt by pilots in this critical battle of World War II. Using revolutionary graphics, Peter Snow gives a blow-by-blow account of the pivotal moments of the battle and how the RAF held off the might of the German Luftwaffe during the summer of 1940. The future of the entire country was at stake in this, the first great air battle in history.

programme.title: The Guns of Navarone
programme.desc: Explosive World War II action yarn in which a group of crack commandos are assembled for an apparently impossible mission. The team, made up of Allied and Greek soldiers with specialist talents, attempt to destroy the seemingly impregnable German artillery units on the Greek island of Navarone and in turn free 2,000 British soldiers on Kiros, an island in the Aegean.

programme.title: Halloween
programme.desc: Classic horror. Fifteen years after murdering his sister, Michael Myers escapes from an asylum and returns to the small town of Haddenfield. Dr Sam Loomis, a psychiatrist who has been treating Michael, races to track him down before he kills again.

programme.title: Hauntings
programme.desc: On the night of Christmas 1998, a homeless man enters the infamous Greyfriars Kirkyard in Edinburgh. Seeking refuge, he breaks into the tomb of George Mackenzie - Edinburgh’s famous executioner - and then falls into an assembly of decomposing corpses. His screams are heard above ground, but something else has been disturbed. Within weeks, stories of blackouts and inexplicable attacks begin to spread. The injuries are so severe that Edinburgh City Council locks the gates and declares the area out of bounds for public safety. Jan Andrew Henderson begins to chronicle the Mackenzie Poltergeist - only to claim to become a target of its malice.

programme.title: Hauntings
programme.desc: In 1958, two young women travel together in a Ford Sedan to a nightclub in Georgia, on the other side of Lake Lanier. But they never return. Weeks later, reports begin of a ghostly figure: a lady wearing a blue dress, walking across the lake, whilst calls for help are heard from the waters below. Then, stories of unexplained drownings emerge. Mysterious deaths at Lake Lanier abound, whilst survivors report the feeling of being pulled into the depths or held beneath by unseen hands.

programme.title: Inside Classical
programme.desc: Join presenter and musician Owain Wyn Evans for a concert full of Halloween tricks and treats. The BBC National Orchestra of Wales, conducted by Ellie Slorach, perform music that is guaranteed to give you a thrill. The concert includes Bach’s gothic masterpiece Toccata and Fugue in D minor, Saint-Saëns Danse Macabre and the spine-tingling Rimsky Korsakov’s arrangement of Mussorgsky’s Night on the Bare Mountain. The orchestra take us to a world of magic and wonderment with film scores by John Williams, including Hedwig’s Theme from Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone, Flying Theme from ET, and the night wouldn’t be complete without one of the most forbidding and recognisable musical scores in cinematic history - The Shark Theme from Jaws!

programme.desc: Another fantastic selection of dance floor disco classics, featuring a wealth of performances from the BBC’s music archives, including Tina Charles, The Real Thing, Sister Sledge and The Bee Gees.

programme.title: Studio 54
programme.desc: In 1970s New York, one nightclub defined an era and a generation. For the first time, Ian Schrager, one of the two people behind the infamous Studio 54, tells the in-depth story of how one of the world’s greatest nightclubs was created. Studio 54 was the epicentre of 70s hedonism - a place that not only redefined the nightclub, but also came to symbolise an entire era. Its co-owners, Ian Schrager and Steve Rubell, two friends from Brooklyn, seemed to come out of nowhere to suddenly preside over a new kind of New York society. Now, 46 years after the velvet rope was first slung across the club’s hallowed threshold, a feature documentary tells the real story behind one of the greatest clubs of all time.

programme.title: Talking Business
programme.desc: Why are record amounts of money pouring into sport? The LA Lakers are starting the new NBA as the most expensive sports team in history after being bought for $12.5bn. Record sums have also been spent on the NFL's Seattle Seahawks and English Premier League teams Liverpool and Chelsea in recent weeks. Is it really being driven by the search for an AI proof investment? Sal Galatioto is the man billionaires call when they want to buy or sell a sports team and he explains why the prices keep on climbing. Leading TV sports rights executive Daniel Cohen, of Octagon Global Media Consulting, explains the impact this is all having on how we watch and how much we pay. Ben Thompson also hears from the billionaire founder and CEO of Fanatics, Michael Rubin, and how fans are continuing to splash out on replica shirts, trading cards and other merchandise.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: This week the BBC announced more cuts as part of its drive to save £500 million, following on from a series of other budget saving measures over the last few months. Katie and Ros take stock of everything announced so far along with a panel of experts: ex-BBC executive Roger Mosey, MP for Southport Patrick Hurley, Baroness Morgan, former Secretary of State for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport and the BBC Deputy Director General Rhodri Talfan-Davies. And a new Channel 4 programme investigates public attitudes toward disability. The creators of The Experiment have built a fictional care home for disabled people and invite members of the public into the facility to see if they can recognise Nazi-era concepts disguised as modern social care. Producer Nick Parnes and presenter Sophie Morgan join the show.

programme.title: The Interface
programme.desc: The show that reaches through your screen, to tell you the tech stories that ready matter. Hosted by BBC technology journalist Thomas Germain and social media expert Professor Jessica Maddox, The Interface dives into the stories, trends, apps, gadgets, algorithms and internet obsessions shaping how we live, work, think and connect. From AI and influencers to memes, data leaks, cybersecurity and the weirdest corners of the web, The Interface explores what happens when technology collides with real life. Cutting through the hype, the hosts unpack the platforms, products and online phenomena that increasingly shape our choices, our culture and our sense of self - whether we like it or not! Sharp, insightful and often very funny, The Interface examines our relationship with technology in all its messy, brilliant, absurd and world-changing glory. Along the way, it tackles one of the biggest questions of our age: what kind of future are the likes of Elon Musk, Chat GPT and all the other Silicon Valley giants building, and does anyone really want to live there?

programme.desc: The best advice from across the series. We hear about the abuse faced by mobility scooter users and find out how a blood test could help ambulance crews identify a stroke faster. Plus, advice on challenging parking fines and making your own cleaner to tackle mould.

programme.title: Crimewatch Caught
programme.desc: A couple and their baby vanish in winter, sparking a nationwide manhunt with a tragic ending. And police hunt a fugitive boasting about his international travels.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Roo Irvine heads to an antiques fair in Detling in Kent. With help from experts Irita Marriott and Nick Hall, the teams hunt for bargains to sell at auction. Meanwhile, Roo takes a look back at the history of crime and punishment.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: In Greater Manchester, upcycling expert Jacqui Joseph explores Altrincham recycling centre, hoping to discover unwanted items that can be revamped or revitalised and sold on for cash. Screen print artist Daniel Heath attempts to brew up a new look for a four-piece coffee table set, upholsterer Ollie Clueit has his hands full with a bulky three-seater sofa, while Jacqui gives a new lease of life to a pair of mid-20th-century deckchairs.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: The sun shines all week long as Alistair Appleton helps a couple to move one step closer to their dream of a new life on the gorgeous Gower Peninsula in Wales. Apart from checking out some fabulous properties, Alistair collects cockles and tries laverbread for the first time.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Mary Louise has made the journey down from Angus, bringing an oak lectern that has valuation expert Simon Bower beguiled. It’s a ‘proper’ antique, which means Ian will always be interested, but exactly how does he plan to fit it in his caravan? The room goes international with our second item of the day, as Stephen comes all the way from Vienna to visit Leith Theatre. He’s bringing a painting by celebrated Lancastrian artist James Isherwood, a name the dealers are sure to recognise. Fans of alliteration will enjoy debonair Duncan’s dinky toys. Condition is king when it comes to these, though, so will he come to regret playing with them in his younger days? Next to face the dealers are sisters Liz and Sharon, selling some heavy gold masonic chains. Usually, scrap metal queen Mel would be the dealer to target, but with new dealers the Rag & Bone Bros in the room, she might face stiff competition. There’s always space for an unusual musical interlude in the room, and today is no different. Jackie has brought along a Balinese gamelan, but will her exotic offering be enough to conjure up a bid from the dealers?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies

programme.desc: For many farmers, summer means one thing - show season - and the Royal Highland Show is the highlight in the calendar. The Barclays boys are showing pedigree Beltex and their finest Suffolks before going head-to-head in the Young Handlers competition. It’s also a major event for budding young farmers Rachel and Camy, who, for the first time, are showing only animals raised on their own farm. Hopes are pinned on their Cheviot lamb Patch to prove she’s every bit as good as Camy predicted. And in Moray, Nikki and Ollie are preparing a show of their own. They’re opening up their farm gates to give the public a taste of what they’re all about.

programme.title: Murder Case
programme.desc: A team of detectives arrive in the market town of Elgin tasked with investigating the brutal murder of a 32-year-old mother of two. On 16 November 2023, Lucretia ‘Kiesha’ Donaghy’s body is discovered in her home after worried friends are unable to reach her. She has been victim of a frenzied attack. We follow the detectives' every move as they search for key evidence and piece together information to uncover the truth of who killed Kiesha. The case quickly unfolds into a complex investigation which demands relentless focus and all of the team’s expertise. Kiesha’s aunt Rachel and her best friend Bob share memories of her vibrant personality, the struggles she faced, and the heartbreak of losing her. With intimate access to the detectives and Kiesha’s loved ones, this episode reveals the personal impact of her murder and the dedicated work involved in seeking justice.

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: The Special Operations Response Team is called to a fall on Arthur’s Seat, where a tourist has been injured near the summit. Paramedics must navigate cragged rocks and scores of hillwalkers to reach their patient, with the help of their most versatile, all-terrain vehicle: the Wolverine. In Aberdeen, student paramedic Amy faces a final assessment on her last training shift. Along with her two senior colleagues, she has to help a drunk man who has fallen over in chaotic circumstances and is making inappropriate comments. They also treat Colin, who is suffering from a serious allergic reaction and in considerable distress. Members of the Special Operations Response team are called to another job, this one just outside Edinburgh, where a man has been injured in an apparent street fight. The team must help coordinate the ambulance response while the police try to control a volatile scene.

St Andrews’ stunning West Sands becomes the sandy beach battleground as three teams of sand-sculpting hopefuls face their toughest challenge yet. Our finalists – Athena and Rachel, Shane and Lisa, and Yusuf and Johannes – have just six hours to create the most ambitious sculptures of their lives before the North Sea sweeps in one last time to claim their masterpieces. Fittingly, the theme is Ultimate Sandcastles – a test of skill, creativity and resilience. Judges Sadie and Jamie are demanding height, arches, spiral staircases and that elusive wow factor. But will our sculptors play it safe or push boundaries to deliver something truly spectacular? Expect drama, collapses, creative differences and plenty of emotion.

Beth decides to cook everything at once and invite Cathy, Colin, Ian, Jaz, Christine and Sophie over to eat it all. Everything goes well until Cathy urges Colin to go next door and get something out of their freezer to replace the defrosted food, a whole Scottish salmon.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: Rehab centres are treating some of their youngest-ever and most physically damaged addicts, and ketamine has been their drug of choice. Stacey Dooley gains rare access to a rehab in Stockport and gets to know former users. Many are in chronic pain, and one young man needs bladder reconstruction surgery. Over four months, she follows them through recovery, relationships, setbacks and celebrations.

programme.title: Matthew Perry and the Ketamine Queen
programme.desc: Documentary investigating events leading up to the shocking death of Friends star Matthew Perry and the woman at the centre of the case, dubbed the 'Ketamine Queen' by US prosecutors. Jasveen Sangha, a drug dealer and dual US-UK citizen, has pleaded guilty to five federal charges in Los Angeles, including one count of distributing ketamine resulting in death or bodily injury. She faces up to 65 years in prison for supplying Perry with the drugs that led to his death. Sangha was one of five people charged in the case. Prosecutors described her home as a 'drug-selling emporium', where authorities found approximately 79 vials of ketamine and other drugs, including methamphetamine, cocaine and Xanax. Presented by Amber Haque, the film features exclusive, first-on-the-record interviews with Sangha's friends and examines her role in Perry’s death and Hollywood’s ketamine drug network.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May conduct a valuable piece of consumer research with their attempts to improve and enhance the ambulance. Starting with a belief that current ambulances, which are usually very big and based on a diesel van, are in need of a rethink, the presenters go their separate ways to focus on the one area they think could be improved. May focuses on passenger comfort, Hammond tries to improve response times by getting other drivers out of the way more effectively, while Clarkson confronts the same issue with the invention of what he calls 'the sports ambulance'. Their three very different creations are then put to the test with a series of severe and often messy challenges, culminating in a fast reaction to a spectacular emergency. Also in this episode, F1 driver Daniel Ricciardo is the star in the Reasonably Priced Car.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson tests the new BMW M3 at the track before switching to another BMW, the space-age, hybrid-powered i8, for a revealing trip up the A1 to Whitby. Also in this programme, Richard Hammond marks the imminent demise of the legendary Land Rover Defender with a heart-stopping attempt to drive one straight up the side of a dam. Meanwhile, James May makes a rare trip to the Top Gear track to test the brand new 500-horsepower Mercedes-AMG GT. The stars in the Reasonably Priced Car are actress Margot Robbie and Hollywood superstar Will Smith.

programme.title: Missing in Paradise: Searching for Sarm
programme.desc: On the night of 7 March 2021, Sarm Heslop disappeared from Siren Song, a luxury charter yacht in the Caribbean where she was living with her boyfriend, Ryan Bane. She hasn’t been seen since. Did Sarm vanish of her own accord? Was there a terrible accident? Or did something more sinister happen? Journalist Tir Dhondy investigates. Tir retraces Sarm's last known movements and tracks down two boat captains whose vessels were moored near the yacht she vanished from. And for the first time, she gets to question Ryan’s account of what happened through his lawyer David Cattie.

programme.title: Zara McDermott
programme.desc: This episode tells the story of Gaia going missing from her aunt’s house just before sunset on a November evening in 2017. Just before she leaves, she makes a last-minute call to her identical twin sister, Maya, then she runs. She’s alone without a coat, phone or medication for her epilepsy and in a state of high distress. After making several emergency calls to police, Gaia’s family believe that a widespread search for her is underway. Days later, after hundreds of volunteers have joined the search, Gaia’s body is found deep in undergrowth on Dancing Ledge. She had died of hypothermia. Zara McDermott wants answers; what or who had she been running from? And could the man that Gaia had briefly been seeing have anything to do with her disappearance?

programme.title: Zara McDermott

programme.title: Zara McDermott

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: Stacey Dooley looks into the deaths of women who have fallen from height, in cases where domestic abuse may have been part of the wider picture, and asks what role, if any, abuse can play in how these women die. As Stacey meets bereaved families, survivors, detectives, lawyers and campaigners, she explores how coercive control can shape women’s lives long before a fatal incident, and whether those histories are given sufficient weight when deaths are investigated. Among the cases, we see Stacey meet the family of Bianca Thomas, a young mother from Birmingham who died after falling from an 11th-floor balcony. Bianca's death was ruled accidental, but her family still have questions about the circumstances surrounding her death. Stacey also hears about the landmark case of Kimberley Milne, whose husband was convicted in Scotland of culpable homicide after sustained domestic abuse was found to have been a significant contributing factor in her death by suicide, and asks what that could mean for similar cases in England and Wales. Powerful and deeply personal, the programme explores grief, justice and the difficult questions surrounding women who die after falling from height.

programme.desc: Cunk continues her ambitious march across the face of mankind into an age of industry and science. She demonstrates the inventions that changed the world and covers how the American Civil War, World War I and World War II taught humanity how to use its new grasp of technology to shoot, blow up and irradiate itself in huge numbers.

programme.title: Cunk on...
programme.desc: In the final episode of her epic journey across history, Philomena Cunk takes us from 1945 to the present day. She travels the world and meets top experts to examine the Cold War, the space race, globalisation and social media. The world's recent history is one of polarisation and division as humanity divided itself down the middle – communism v capitalism, Apple v Microsoft, Beatles v Stones. Is humanity doomed to repeat the mistakes of history? Cunk does her best to find out.

We join him at home and get a good look around as he reveals his creepiest moments - a Tudor family show us the extent of their ghostly superstitions and the Vikings demonstrate how to become truly terrifying to your enemies. Death himself is joined by some rather creepy friends to sing about his favourite scary things.

programme.title: Death in Paradise
programme.desc: Mervin and the team investigate the murder of a local newspaper’s notorious agony aunt, poisoned the morning after her retirement party while reading her final advice column. The paperboy is swiftly ruled out, but the police are left stumped when he insists he delivered the stack of papers at random. Nobody else in the neighbourhood was taken ill, so how could the killer have ensured the victim would pick up the only poisoned copy? Meanwhile, Mervin resists the counselling sessions Selwyn has imposed after the case in Antigua. And as he grapples with his feelings towards his brother, Mervin gets a rude awakening from an unexpected figure. Is blood really thicker than water?

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: It’s Halloween in Finglas, and everyone is getting into the spooky spirit of things. Agnes is ready for the trick or treaters, but she gets more than she bargained for when she receives a surprising visitor from her past. As no-one else can see her ghostly guest, they think she’s gone mad - not even Doctor Flynn can help. Luckily, Father Damien is on hand, and with a little help from Grandad, they get rid of the unwanted guest in time to head down to Foley’s for a fancy-dress party.

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: The new year starts badly when Winnie’s place is burgled and her mother’s much-loved wedding ring is missing. Meanwhile, Cathy is worried about her impending birthday.

programme.title: The Traitors Ireland
programme.desc: Siobhán McSweeney welcomes a group of strangers to Slane Castle to play the ultimate murder mystery game. Siobhán picks her Traitors, but this time, there’s a twist that causes immediate confusion amongst the group. One player emerges a hero from the mission, but has this put a target on their back? The Traitors meet for the first time.

programme.title: The Traitors Ireland
programme.desc: The doors of Slane Castle have opened once again, with 23 new players entering The Traitors Ireland for its second season. The line-up features contestants from across the country, ranging in age from 24 to 61 and including teachers, a postal worker, a psychotherapist, a musician, a stay-at-home dad, an Irish Defence Forces member, and an actor and drama teacher. Hosted once again by Siobhán McSweeney, the players attempt to navigate a game built on trust, strategy and deception, forming alliances while trying to work out who among them they can believe.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: How do you protect Britain’s busiest mountain when more than 600,000 people visit each year? Charlotte Smith and Joe Crowley head to Yr Wyddfa, Wales’s highest peak, to meet the people caring for its landscape and keeping visitors on the move. Joe joins volunteers tackling litter in some of the mountain’s hardest-to-reach gullies before discovering work to protect rare alpine plants and the elusive Snowdon beetle, found nowhere else in the UK. Meanwhile, Charlotte goes behind the scenes at Wales’s highest cafe to find out what it takes to keep visitors fed and watered at the summit. And Tom Heap investigates how organised crime gangs are targeting the countryside.

programme.title: The Celebrity Traitors
programme.desc: As a new day dawns, breakfast brings a fresh shock for the Faithful. In the mission, the celebrity players are taken to a mysterious location where the Traitors must work as a team under tense circumstances. Back at the castle, have the Faithful gathered credible leads to topple a Traitor, or are they being hoodwinked further away from the truth?

programme.title: The Celebrity Traitors: Uncloaked
programme.desc: Exclusive chat from the latest banished and murdered players to leave the castle, with Ed Gamble. Plus, see the delicious reactions as they find out the identity of the Traitors for the first time.

programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. programme.title: Clive Myrie’s Caribbean Adventure
programme.desc: In Jamaica’s capital city, Clive learns he has hidden talents when it comes to trying out some dancehall moves. He explores a 19th-century mansion which tells the story of Jamaica’s first black millionaire and heads to the school that has produced most of the country’s Olympic sprinting talent. Clive also makes time to head for the hills to sample a special Jamaican-Irish stout punch as he learns of the long connection between these two islands.

It's Scotland versus Southport, with the teams clashing over such fiendish questions as: what would come fourth in the following sequence, 7: 1111111, 5: SEVEN, 3: VII…?

programme.title: See Hear
programme.desc: See Hear celebrates Black History Month with a special programme exploring 2026’s theme of honouring communities. Through personal stories of heritage, identity, resilience and belonging, we meet people from the black deaf community reflecting on their experiences, the challenges they have faced and the importance of representation. Presenter Ahmed Mudawi is joined in the studio by Sandra Campbell, a former deaf athlete who now works for the British Deaf Association. Sandra shares her family’s Jamaican heritage and reflects on the experiences of her great-grandmother, grandmother and mother, whose journeys helped shape her own life. generations.

Baker Briony May Williams is in North Yorkshire to find which potato makes the perfect chip, and chef Suzie Lee is in County Down, finding out exactly what goes into making scampi. And with lots of people now working from home, chef Julie Lin is on the hunt for healthy snacks.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael’s exploration of Essex continues in Romford. He arrives on the London Overground’s Liberty Line to visit a state-of-the-art rail-operating centre responsible for the whole of the East Anglian rail network. He discovers how signallers and operators control the movements of over 4,000 trains a day and learns how they respond to emergencies on the tracks. At Upminster, he finds the gateway to the Chafford Gorges Nature Park, which for centuries was exploited for its natural resources. The former chalk quarries have been transformed into a rare habitat for orchids, and he hears how archaeologists have discovered Neanderthal stone tools in the chalky cliffs. Michael takes a scenic rail journey through the marshy landscape of the Dengie Peninsula to arrive at a marina on the River Blackwater. He makes a choppy crossing to visit the Ross Revenge ship, home to Radio Caroline since the 1980s.

programme.title: Earth’s Tropical Islands
programme.desc: A journey from Borneo's rich coral reefs, through lush jungles to its mountainous heart, revealing why this island is home to a greater variety of life than almost any other.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team return to King's College, Cambridge. Finds include a papal portrait, early maps of America and a machine gun from the First World War.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! is at Blackburn Cathedral in the centre of Blackburn in Lancashire. The cathedral was completed in 1926, formally the Church of St Mary. Experts Charles Hanson and Philip Serrell are on hand to find a selection of objects to take to auction. Charles values a wooden Fijian club, while two vintage enamel signs catch Philip’s eye. Paul Martin takes a look at the impressive Talbot collection – local press photographs taken of events, celebrities and the royal family over a 50-year period.

programme.desc: The Hairy Bikers are back in Scotland, but this time, they're in the beautiful region of Dumfries and Galloway. It’s another place close to Dave and Si’s hearts, a rural paradise with a glorious coastline that stretches for more than 200 miles which they used to visit 30 years ago.

programme.desc: A brutal murder in an Inverness home sparks a manhunt for two violent suspects. Detectives recover crucial evidence beside a canal and track down CCTV, but the case takes a strange turn when they begin to doubt their main eyewitness. On Lewis, police face a stand-off with a camper van driver who insists the law doesn’t apply to her. And in the Cairngorms, an upturned canoe triggers a search for a missing man.

programme.title: Surgeons: At the Edge of Life

Golf brought Bill to Ireland, but the best moments often happen far from the course.

When a desperate patient unexpectedly shows up at their home seeking help, he leaves behind a terrifying supernatural entity that preys on families and feeds on the suffering of its victims. Film horror from the mind of Stephen King.

programme.desc: Today, Flog It! comes from Oxburgh Hall in Norfolk. Six antiques experts are on hand to find a selection of objects to take to auction. Anita Manning discovers a Victorian dynamometer used for measuring the pressure of steam, and David Harper is taken back to the days of ocean liners with a wine stopper from 1912. Paul Martin visits Cromer to find out about the RNLI’s most decorated lifeboatman.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob travel to the River Ribble in Lancashire for one last fish with their little canine pal, Ted. The beautiful river Ribble runs through the rolling hills of the Yorkshire Dales, onwards to Lancashire before meeting the Irish Sea in Lytham. With the river in good health, Paul and Bob hope to catch a good chub or a mighty barbel on this stretch of the water, while Ted hopes to taste Bob’s Lancashire hotpot.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: Experts claim that artificial intelligence has begun to exhibit early signs of agency. What does the rise of the superintelligence mean for society? Is humanity on a path to superintelligence or hurtling towards self-destruction? Professor Hannah Fry explores the promises and threats of AI, considering the ways in which superintelligent machines could help humanity as well as the ways in which they could be a hindrance. Over the course of the episode, a range of experts discuss the future of humanity in the age of AI.

programme.title: The Secret Genius of Modern Life
programme.desc: Hannah Fry takes a look at the bank card, the digital key to accessing cash, and finds out how its extraordinary innovations have some surprising and sinister origins.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: The Bear Ladies restore a stuffed monkey that turned royal heads. The team also fix a cake topper emblematic of a circus childhood and a Second World War helmet that survived the Blitz.

programme.title: Murder in Belfast: Sisters Seeking Justice
programme.desc: The killing of Robert McCartney erupted from nowhere: a Sunday night at a city pub ended in a gang attack and murder. As evidence vanishes, Robert’s family aren’t getting any answers. There is a race to find out what happened from the survivor of the stabbing - but the police aren’t the only organisation trying to talk to witnesses.

programme.title: Ellie & Natasia
programme.desc: A routine driving lesson takes a bizarre, surreal turn; a game show called Find the Snakes is destined to sweep the nation; contemporary politicians are introduced to a literal public arena; vape sommeliers treat e-liquid profiles with the gravity of a fine Bordeaux; two ultra-wealthy girls are determined to get exactly what they want; and two restaurant-goers take their love of food to an intense extreme. Featuring an appearance from Asim Chaudry.

programme.title: Unspun World with John Simpson
programme.desc: Unspun World provides an unvarnished version of the week's major global news stories - reliable, honest and essential viewing. The BBC's world affairs editor, John Simpson, brings his experience and expertise to bear on the most important international stories. In discussion with the BBC's unparalleled range of experts across the world, he uses their unique local knowledge to go beyond the headlines to get to the unspun truth about the world.

programme.title: Escaping Idi Amin
programme.desc: In August 1972, Idi Amin is 18 months into his dictatorship. Supporters hail the new president - a former boxer and soldier - as a saviour, and his rise to power is greeted with celebration and hope across Uganda. But beneath the apparent social harmony, resentment runs deep. Until 1962, Uganda had been a protectorate of the British - with the British very much at the top of the pile, Africans at the bottom and Asians in the middle. Despite ten years of independence, many Africans feel that they are denied opportunities to improve their position in society. Idi Amin decides to exploit their feelings and increase support for his regime. With one announcement from the president, the lives of 80,000 people in Uganda are changed forever. In a bid to cement his leadership, Idi Amin announces that all Ugandan Asians must leave the country within 90 days. Will they be able to flee on their British passports?

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Bordeaux’s world-famous vineyards are undergoing a revival as vintners seek to update their wines by introducing new technology and reinventing older traditions. Eva visits Saint-Emilion, where wine production began 1,000 years ago, and enjoys unusual wine pairings - a deep red with fish and a buttery white with cheese. But Bordeaux isn’t just about wine; it has superb produce, including succulent duck and tender beef as well as 200-million-year-old caviar, served with signature bordelaise sauces.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: The seasons are changing at Longmeadow, and Monty is planting spring-flowering bulbs to provide colour and interest in the months ahead. It’s also time to clear the greenhouse to make space for winter storage. Adam Frost visits RHS Harlow Carr to see how the newly renovated borders are flourishing. Arit Anderson talks to members of the Coco Collective, who grow and cook food from their inner-city allotment, and Sue Kent is at home creating a new planting scheme for next spring. In Oxfordshire, grower Andy Howard shares his passion for the heritage apples thriving in his back garden micro nursery.

programme.title: See Hear
programme.desc: See Hear celebrates the beautiful game, exploring deaf football, the fight for accessibility and the inspiring people breaking down barriers on and off the pitch. In the studio, presenter Ahmed Mudawi welcomes Oliver Eadsforth, a passionate advocate for deaf football who works with the England and Great Britain teams, supporting players and helping develop the game on and off the pitch. Oliver reflects on his lifelong love of football, from playing goalkeeper at school and university to taking on roles in administration, player development and international football. He discusses the progress made in deaf sport, the importance of having a voice in decision-making and why more opportunities are needed for deaf people to become coaches and leaders.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s exploration of Essex reaches Chelmsford. At a huge construction site on the outskirts of the city he discovers Beaulieu Park, the first railway station to be built on the Great Eastern Main Line for over 100 years. Michael learns how the station is designed to alleviate congestion in Chelmsford city centre. At Chelmsford Cathedral, the headquarters of the diocese of Chelmsford, Michael meets the bishop of Chelmsford, the Rt Revd Dr Guli Francis-Dehqani. He discovers one of the largest and most diverse dioceses in England and hears Bishop Guli’s extraordinary personal story of escape from Iran after the Islamic revolution of 1979. Michael continues his rail journey on the Great Eastern Main Line and visits the historic riverside town of Maldon, with its pretty Thames barges. Michael learns about a medieval battle and handles a rare Viking sword. He finishes this leg of his Essex journey in the coastal village of Tollesbury, with its strong maritime heritage and marshy landscape, a haven for birds and wildlife.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Arriving in the Essex market town of Witham, Michael heads into the countryside to visit Terling Place, one of the county’s great country houses. He hears how in the late 19th century, Victorian scientist the 3rd Baron Rayleigh discovered the atmospheric gas argon here. Michael joins the Braintree branch line - aka the Flitch line - and alights at Cressing to visit two huge medieval barns that are thought to be the oldest timber-framed structures in England. At Braintree, Michael learns about the town's wool and silk industries before heading to the Warner and Sons archive, where he discovers a depository of thousands of silk patterns, including two pieces with a royal connection. At Great Bardfield, Michael traces a group of artists including Edward Bawden and Eric Ravilious, who settled in the pretty Essex village from the 1930s onwards. He meets the author of a book on the artists, who now lives in their former home.

programme.title: Secrets of the Aquarium
programme.desc: Marcus, the new curator, attempts a high-risk move for a problem shark to the top of the aquarium. Andrew builds a cave for a reclusive lobster, and star attraction Friday the turtle suffers a nasty bite from a mystery tankmate.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team head to Abergavenny in Wales. Also, a bizarre coincidence unites two Beatles collectors.

programme.title: Flog It!

programme.title: Uncanny
programme.desc: In the final case of the series, Danny is joined in the studio by Angela and her daughter Emily. They tell him about events that happened to them in the early 2000s when Emily was a child. A seemingly supernatural presence that began as what Angela thought was an imaginary friend, soon grew into something far more terrifying. Both Emily and her sister became too scared to sleep in their rooms, supposedly beset by the malign presence of an old man who threatened Emily and her family. When Angela’s friends and babysitters began to experience things too, refusing to return to the house, Angela worried for the safety of her daughter. Events escalated to the point where the family felt they were physically in danger. It all seems beyond belief until Danny investigates the history of the house and makes a shocking discovery. As ever, the audience is invited to share their theories and help crack the case.

Professor Hannah Fry explores the promises and threats of AI, considering the ways in which superintelligent machines could help humanity as well as the ways in which they could be a hindrance. Over the course of the episode, a range of experts discuss the future of humanity in the age of AI.
